version.value: The six songs for voice and piano (Le Dromadaire, La Chèvre du Thibet, La Sauterelle, Le Dauphin, L’Écrevisse, La Carpe); the edition is not stated.
version.note: The dealer’s supplement lists the six titles and says the composer is at the piano. Johnson’s note gives the six poems as numbers 10, 4, 17, 19, 22 and 23 of Apollinaire’s collection. The printed edition used by the performers is not named.

performers.note: The Internet Archive item credits Pierre Bernac and Francis Poulenc and lists baritone and piano; the 1947 supplement says “with the composer at the piano”.

date.note: The record was listed as an import by April 1947 and appears in a numbered list of reviewed records in The Gramophone of September 1947, with a reference to the August issue, p. 34. The session date is not given in the sources consulted.

place.note: No source consulted names the studio.

label.note: The supplement lists a 12-inch imported record, No. G-DB6299, with Montparnasse on the other side.

catalogue.note: The Internet Archive label data read “D.B.6299”; the list in The Gramophone reads “H.M.V. DB6299”.

matrixTakeSides.value: 2EA 10804-1 (Le Bestiaire); Montparnasse on the other side, 2EA 10807-1
matrixTakeSides.note: From the item description of this side and of the separate transfer of the Montparnasse side. The take number of the matrix is as given by the transferring archive.

credits.value: George Blood, L.P., for the Great 78 Project (Internet Archive); disc from the Bowling Green collection
credits.note: The item description names the engineer’s firm and lists the collections georgeblood and 78rpm_bowling_green.

date.value: Not stated; the item was made public on 3 November 2023
date.note: The public date of the item is an upload date, not the date of the transfer.

processing.value: Four stylus sizes were tried; the preferred version was equalised with turnover 375 Hz and roll-off −12 dB, and copied under the friendlier file name.
processing.note: As stated in the item description. The published MP3 is the Internet Archive derivative of that file.

digital.format: Internet Archive derivative MP3 from a FLAC transfer

composition.value: Poulenc died in 1963, so the music is in copyright in the EU under the life-plus-70 term, which runs to the end of 2033; national wartime extensions, which can lengthen the term for older works in France, were not assessed. The 1911 text is by Apollinaire, who died in 1918; rights in the poems are not assessed here.
composition.note: Rights in the composition are stated separately from rights in the recording. The United States status of the music is not established here.

recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial EU public domain: first published before 1963; on sale as an import by April 1947 and reviewed in The Gramophone in 1947.
recording.note: The United States status of a recording made in France in the 1940s is not established.
